decision.title: The allocator interface has no reallocate

body.p: (task 0.5). sxml_allocator_operations has allocate and only, as in docs/C_GUIDELINES.md. A reallocate would need the old size and alignment in its request, every host allocator (JavaScript, Swift, Kotlin) would have to implement it, and the main grower, the arena, grows by adding blocks. Growable arrays allocate anew and copy, geometrically, which is amortized O(1). Interfaces are not extended in place, so if profiling shows a need, a new interface type is published. allocate rejects 0 (SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT), avoiding malloc(0)'s implementation-defined result. The wrappers check every request, so implementations may trust their arguments, and sxml_allocator_allocate also checks the alignment of what an implementation returns. An allocator with operations == NULL is the null allocator: "this object must not grow". The default allocator uses malloc up to alignof(max_align_t) and aligned_alloc above it (size rounded up to the alignment for C libraries that still require it); on Windows it uses _aligned_malloc for everything, since _aligned_free cannot release malloc memory.
